text:
sasha: Quick design ping — thinking out loud about adding microqueue pacing + small per-tenant slab allocation to the continuous batcher to reduce oscillation/eviction storms. Looking for quick takes on complexity vs win. :thinking:

kevin: short take: sounds promising. biggest risk is added scheduling churn and harder-to-reason-about fairness. how do you plan to measure? :eyes:

sasha: metrics: batch fill rate, p50/p95 token latency, queue residency distribution, eviction rate, effective headroom per tenant. also need to capture burst recovery time and CPU/GPU utilization variance.

li: can you sketch the runtime model? i.e., tokens-per-second pacing or slot-based?

sasha: prototype idea: two levers — 1) soft pacing tokens (token bucket per tenant) that limit enqueue pace into coalesce window, 2) micro-slab reservation: keep N small "fast slots" per tenant (configurable by tier) which bypass normal eviction for tiny windows. both are soft: can steal from shared pool when idle.

anna: does slab mean fixed slot count or byte/token budget? if fixed slots, risk of wasted capacity on low-util tenants.

sasha: good point — slab as a tiny credit budget (tokens) that replenishes slowly. slot semantics are simpler for fairness math though. tradeoff: simpler invariants vs efficiency.

kevin: how would this interact with preemption and canary fallback? if slab holds requests and a GPU node goes away we could have a big shuffle. need deterministic drain path.

sasha: plan for graceful drain: slab credits drain first to shared pool, and pacing stops allowing immediate enqueue to general pool. fallback policy: canary model uses lower slab quotas initially.

li: want to see config prototype. also need to ensure observability hooks — per-tenant slab-usage, pacing-blocked-rate, reclaim events.

sasha: draft config prototype (very rough):

```
batcher:
  microqueue:
    pacing_rate: 500 # tokens/sec per tenant default
    slab_budget: 64   # tokens reserved as fast-path
    slab_replenish: 1m
    stealable_from_slab: true
    eviction_policy: LRU_soft
```

kevin: that looks reasonable. for experiments we should run A/B across a subset of tenants with synthetic microbursts (short 20-200 token requests) and several real workloads. capture p99 latency and tail of batch sizes.

anna: operational concerns: increased config surface. suggest sane defaults and auto-tune: e.g., set pacing_rate based on moving average of token rate per tenant * 1.5, slab_budget proportional to 0.5 * p95 batch size.

sasha: yes — auto-tune is on the roadmap. immediate next step: instrument current continuous batcher to emit the metrics li asked for (per-tenant slab-like counters so we can simulate). kevin/anna can you own two parts? kevin: synthetic load harness + AB runner. anna: telemetry + alert rules.

kevin: I can take the harness. will spin up a small benchmark and post results in 48h.

anna: I'll add metrics and a dashboard tile. alert thresholds: >5% eviction_rate increase or +20% p95 tokens latency for test tenants.

li: will we need a small RFC? this is bigger than a bugfix.

sasha: yeah — i'll draft a short RFC after the first bench that covers invariants, failure modes, and rollout plan. aiming for RFC by next week if bench looks good.

ci-bot: CI run queued for branch "microqueue-proto" — build 1423 started. :rocket:

kevin: cool. i'll link the benchmark harness and sample workloads in the RFC.

sasha: thanks all. main goal is reducing eviction storm and smoothing tail latency without hurting throughput. will follow up with numbers. :thumbsup:
